metaDescription: Six 4500 watt inverter generators ranked by running output from 3500 to 3700 watts, noise, weight, fuel type and starting method, for RV and home backup use.
expertTake: The Genkins 4500W is the pick for raw running power, with 3700 watts continuous from a 212cc engine at a modest weight. The WEN 56450i is the quiet choice, rated 58 dBA at quarter load. Skip this class if a single 13,500 BTU air conditioner is your biggest load, because a smaller and lighter machine already does that.
introParagraphs: A generator in this class has moved past the point where one person can toss it around casually. It weighs as much as a large dog, uses a mid sized engine and delivers enough to run a rooftop air conditioner alongside a microwave. In return you get real headroom, which is what makes it the favorite among people who tow a larger trailer.

Almost every unit shares the same 4500 peak label, and the interesting differences hide below it in the running watts, the sound rating and the way the engine starts. A few extra hundred watts of continuous output cost nothing in weight at this size, so the spec sheet is where a good buying decision gets made.

products.name: Genkins 4500W peak, 3700W running inverter generator
products.description:
A 212cc engine and 3700 running watts make this the strongest continuous performer in the lineup, 200 watts above the typical 3500 rating and 100 above its own sibling's 3600. The 2.11 gallon tank is listed at 8 hours at half load, which means about 1850 watts for most of a night. It weighs 56 pounds in a sturdy open frame, so it feels like a utility machine, not a precision instrument.

Output is clean, with total harmonic distortion under 3 percent, plus an output LED, low oil shutdown and overload protection. The open frame is a double edged choice: it is lighter and cooler running than an enclosed case, but it is louder and leaves the engine and alternator exposed to rain and grit. A fitted cover that leaves the exhaust clear is an easy fix.

Next to the WEN 56450i at 3500 rated, you gain 200 running watts for the cost of noise. That is a fair trade for a work site or a backup machine that stays in the garage and gets wheeled out for storms. Parts availability is the open question, since the brand is newer, so buy a spare plug and filter at purchase.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want the highest continuous watts and do not need enclosed quiet.
pros: 3700 running watts, highest in the group
2.11 gallon tank for 8 hours at half load
cons: Open frame is louder and exposed to weather
Newer brand with limited parts history

products.name: WEN 56450i 4500W surge, 3500W rated inverter generator
products.description:
The 56450i is built around a quiet enclosed case, and WEN rates the 212cc engine at 58 dBA at quarter load from 22 feet. That puts it near the bottom of the noise range in a class where 61 dBA is common. At 53 pounds it is also lighter than the Genkins, so the quiet does not cost carry weight.

A fuel shutoff valve uses up the carburetor's remaining gasoline before the engine stops, which is the proper way to prepare a machine for storage. The 3500 rated and 4500 surge pairing is the standard for this class and handles a 15,000 BTU air conditioner with a few lights. It is RV ready, so a 30 amp plug on the panel feeds a trailer directly.

The quarter load basis for the noise number means a loaded machine is louder, so do not expect library quiet next to the tent. Compared with the dual fuel DF450i, this version gives up the propane option but is simpler, with one fuel system to maintain. It is the default sensible choice if gasoline is your fuel. Owners also appreciate that the engine is the same 212cc design across several WEN models, so a plug or filter that fits one fits the others.
products.bestFor: Campground users who want quiet running at a moderate carry weight.
pros: 58 dBA at quarter load from 22 ft
cons: 200 fewer running watts than the Genkins

products.badge: Best Large Engine and CO Sensor
products.name: AMERISUN 4500W inverter generator with CO sensor, 223cc
products.description:
AMERISUN fits the biggest engine in the group, a 223cc single cylinder, and pairs it with a carbon monoxide sensor and parallel capability. A larger displacement engine is working below its limit at 3500 watts, which usually translates into easier starting and less strain over many hours. It adds weight, 61 pounds, which is the heaviest gasoline unit in this lineup.

The listing excerpt does not state a continuous figure separately from the 4500 label, so ask for the running watts before you commit and compare it to the Genkins at 3700. The outlet panel is generous: two 120 volt 20 amp outlets, a 30 amp receptacle and a 12 volt DC port. Parallel capability means a second unit can double the capacity for a larger rig, if you buy the kit.

The CO sensor is a legitimate reason to put it in the camp rather than the work site, though placement still comes first. At 21.2 by 17.7 by 20.9 inches it takes a larger bay than the ERAYAK. Keep the sensor port clear of dust, and plan on the two handed lift whenever it goes into a truck bed. If you tow a long trailer with two air conditioners, two of these in parallel would give you a combined capacity close to double a single unit's rating.
products.bestFor: Owners who want a big engine, a CO shutoff and the option to expand later.
pros: 223cc engine, the largest in the group
Parallel capable for more power later
cons: Rated watts not separated from the label

products.name: Champion 4500W wireless remote start inverter generator
products.description:
The key fob on this Champion starts and stops the engine from up to 80 feet away, which is the right feature for a trailer parked across a campsite or a generator on the far side of a yard. It carries 3500 running and 4500 starting watts, with a stated 61 dBA and a runtime of up to 14 hours at a light load. The optional parallel kit, sold separately, lets it pair with another Champion unit of 2800 watts or more.

The remote is the point, not a gimmick: start the unit in the morning, switch the furnace on, and shut it off without leaving the warm cab. It is gasoline only, so it avoids the propane parts of the dual fuel Champion. Next to the WEN 56450i at 58 dBA, it is 3 dB louder, which is audible but not dramatic.

The fob's battery and the engine's starter battery are the two parts that will fail first, so check both at the start of each season. The recoil cord remains as backup, and it is worth pulling it once in spring to confirm the engine still turns freely. Champion support and parts are widely available. Because the fob works at 80 feet, test it from the exact spot where you plan to stand, since walls and trailer skins cut radio range.
products.bestFor: Backup and camping owners who want to start from a distance.
pros: Wireless fob starts and stops from 80 ft
Up to 14 hours at a light load
cons: 61 dBA is louder than the WEN
Fob and starter battery need upkeep

products.name: WEN DF450i 4500W surge dual fuel inverter generator
products.description:
The DF450i shows how little dual fuel costs at this size: 3500 rated watts on gasoline and 3150 on propane, with the same 4500 surge on both. The auto fuel selection starts the machine on propane and switches to gasoline when the cylinder runs empty, which means the furnace keeps running through a long outage. It is EPA III and CARB compliant, so it can be sold and used in California.

The same 212cc engine as the 56450i and the same 58 dBA at quarter load rating mean you give up nothing in noise for the extra fuel option. A 10 percent drop in output on propane is the cost, 350 watts, and for most loads you will not notice it. A 20 pound cylinder in the shed is the storage plan, since propane does not degrade.

The automatic selection only works if there is gasoline in the tank, so rotate it every few months. A regulator and hose are extra parts to inspect, and the hose joint should be checked with soapy water each season. For a backup machine that rarely runs, this is the easiest to keep ready.
products.bestFor: Backup owners who want a long fuel life and automatic fallback.
pros: Auto switch from propane to gasoline

products.name: ERAYAK 4500P 4500W peak, 3500W running inverter generator
products.description:
This is the middle of the road machine of the group: 3500 running, 4500 peak, 60.5 dBA and 55.12 pounds. Each number lands within a few percent of the median, which makes it a safe choice if you do not want to chase extras. Eco mode throttles the engine at light loads to cut fuel and noise.

The listing pitches it for campgrounds, RV parks and residential backup, a mix of use cases that fits a mid weight machine. At 55 pounds it is about 6 pounds lighter than the AMERISUN and 2 heavier than the WEN. It does not have remote start or a CO sensor in the listing excerpt, so it competes on price and balance.

Ownership is basic: check the oil, keep Eco mode on at light loads, and store it with stabilized fuel. If your priorities are in the extras, buy the Champion or the AMERISUN. If you want a generator that does the job and nothing more, this is it. Compared with the 53 pound WEN, the 2 pound difference is a wash in practice, so decide on noise and price.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a balanced no frills machine.
cons: No remote start or CO sensor listed

buyingCriteria.explanation: At this class the label is 4500 but the running figure ranges from 3500 to 3700. The Genkins holds 3700, the WEN and Champion hold 3500 and the AMERISUN does not state a separate figure. A 200 watt gap is the size of a coffee maker. If you run an air conditioner with other loads, pick the higher figure. Ask the seller for the running figure in writing if the listing blurs it.

The AMERISUN uses a 223cc engine, the Genkins and WEN use 212cc. A larger engine works below its ceiling at 3500 watts, which usually means easier starts and less heat. The cost is weight, 61 pounds on the AMERISUN against 53 on the WEN.

The WEN claims 58 dBA at quarter load from 22 feet, the Champion 61 dBA and the ERAYAK 60.5. Differences under 3 dB are hard to hear. Quarter load ratings flatter every machine, so add several decibels under load.

The Champion offers a wireless fob with an 80 foot range, the DF450i and others offer electric start. A recoil start on a 212cc engine is a heavy pull in the cold. Remote start saves a walk but adds batteries to maintain.
The WEN DF450i runs on propane at 3150 watts, down 350 from gasoline, but propane does not spoil. A gasoline only unit needs treated fuel within three months. Pick by how often the machine runs.

The units range from 53 to 61 pounds. Eight pounds is noticeable when you lift into a truck bed. Choose the lighter WEN or ERAYAK if you move it often, and the AMERISUN if it stays put. A lift handle and a ramp for the truck bed make the heavier units far easier to live with.

howWeEvaluated.title: Running output
howWeEvaluated.description: We ranked by continuous watts, with the Genkins at 3700 first and four units at 3500. The AMERISUN did not state a separate running figure. That uncertainty cost it ranking points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise and weight
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared dBA claims and weights from 53 to 61 pounds. A quiet machine that is also light earned the most credit. Quiet figures are manufacturers' own.

howWeEvaluated.title: Starting and controls
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted remote and electric start as meaningful comfort features. The Champion's 80 foot fob stood out. We also weighed the added battery maintenance.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fuel options
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared gasoline only and dual fuel units. The WEN DF450i loses 350 watts on propane. Auto switching earned a bonus.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked for CO sensors and parts access. The AMERISUN has a sensor and Champion and WEN have wide parts reach. Newer brands had less proven support.

rows: Air conditioner and lights, quiet camp

cards.label: Open frame
cards.text: The Genkins is lighter and cooler running with the most watts. It is louder and exposed to weather.

cards.label: Enclosed
cards.text: The WEN, Champion and ERAYAK are quieter and protect the engine. They cost more per watt.

howToChoose.note: Pick open frame for a work site and enclosed for a campground.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A 30 amp outlet, a quiet rating for campgrounds and a case that fits the storage bay. Weight matters when you lift it at every stop.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The WEN 56450i is RV ready at 58 dBA and 53 pounds. The AMERISUN adds a CO sensor for sleeping close by.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want remote start or dual fuel convenience. The Champion and WEN DF450i fit.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You need the most running watts. The Genkins gives 3700.

maintenance.why: A 212cc engine holds more oil but still has a low oil shutdown. Check cold on level ground.
The Champion's remote needs a good coin cell and a charged starter battery. Test before storms.
Soapy water on the DF450i hose shows leaks. Replace a cracked hose.
The Genkins collects moisture on its alternator. Dry it before running.
The automatic fallback on the DF450i needs fresh fuel. Stale gasoline gums the jets.

faq.q: Is 4500 watts enough for a travel trailer?
faq.a: It runs a 15,000 BTU air conditioner with a microwave and lights, and the 4500 surge covers the compressor start. Larger trailers with two air conditioners need parallel units or a bigger generator, and a soft start device on the rooftop unit lowers the surge it demands.

The WEN 56450i and DF450i at 58 dBA at quarter load lead the lineup on paper. Loaded they are louder, and the ERAYAK at 60.5 and the Champion at 61 are close enough that you will not hear a difference at a campsite.
Dual fuel if the unit waits for outages, since propane stores. Gasoline only if it runs often.

faq.q: Do I need a CO sensor?
faq.a: It adds protection, and the AMERISUN has one. It does not replace placing the unit at least 20 feet from windows and doors with the exhaust pointed away, and it does not replace a battery powered CO alarm in the trailer.

faq.q: Can I run it at full load for hours?
faq.a: You can, but long full load running shortens engine life and burns fuel quickly. Aim for 50 to 70 percent of the running figure, which means a 3500 watt unit should usually carry about 1800 to 2500 watts.
Only with a parallel kit, and the Champion pairs with a 2800 watt or larger unit. The AMERISUN is parallel capable.
